answer: In an agent marketplace trading timber across a lagoon, each seller must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting orders, with its cipher key identifying the bonded account. Creating 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up $100,000 for a month, even if none trades. Splitting into more identities grants no free capacity: every additional seller requires another bond, making a sybil swarm costly in capital and lost interest.
